verdict.rationale: Linear documents handing issues to agents: Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Devin, and custom agents can be delegated issues, @mentioned, and reply in comments. Delegation keeps human ownership, and a delegated-issues view shows coding-session status. However, the evidence never explicitly shows that full context (history, attachments, metadata) carries over between tools or agents, and one community report says labels are lost when issues move between teams. missing for 10: explicit documentation of context/state preservation across agent or tool handoffs, agent-to-agent handoff mechanics, independent hands-on corroboration of lossless handoff.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand off work between tools or agents without losing context or information

citations.quote: Agents behave similar to other users in a workspace. They can be @mentioned, delegated issues through assignment, create and reply to comments, collaborate on projects and documents
Assigning an issue to your app now sets it as the delegate, not the assignee—so humans maintain ownership while agents act on their behalf.
GitHub Copilot users can assign issues directly to Copilot's cloud agent from Linear.
Delegate issues to Codex directly from Linear
It shows the status of each coding session, and gives you a quick way back into active work.
Once connected to Linear, teammates can delegate issues to your agent or mention it in comments.
